No. The 67.7 ha loss is dated 2020, which falls before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so it is outside the post-cut-off interval. It appears in the evidence as history, not as a post-baseline event.

For 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-31, no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected across the whole 2843.1 ha asset. Hansen data covered 100% of the property. Only 0.4 ha of loss in small patches (under 0.5 ha) was seen in 2021, and those patches are not counted as events.

Limits: changes under 0.5 ha, at edges, or narrower than the 30 m pixels may be missed. This is not a compliance finding, so it does not establish that the property is EUDR compliant or deforestation-free. One more caution: Hansen records loss by year, so the 2020 date doesn't show whether the loss happened before or after 31 December 2020. The evidence places it in the pre-baseline period.
